lines.text: They came in the morning, through the smoke. Twelve riders in blue, with silver lenses at their throats.
The village did its best. Our blacksmith coughed. Our farmers limped. One of the goats, for reasons nobody could ever explain, also limped.
What a charming festival. I don't believe I've ever seen one quite like it.
Ancient tradition, Magister. Very old. Very sacred.
How old?
Older than me.
Ilse! My best student. You've been gone so long, the College thought the wolves had eaten you.
Magister Hask. I found nothing here. A cold village, and a boy who reads too many books.
Then you won't mind if I look.
Welcome to Greyhollow, Magister. I'm Lucan Varr.
He raised his lens to look at me. It fogged over at once. He wiped it on his sleeve, and looked again. It fogged again.
This damp northern air. It gets into everything.
By writ of the Grand Measurer, the Order will measure every soul in Greyhollow. Every man, every woman, every child.
Behind him, the youngest of the twelve, a girl not much older than me, was staring at Ash with her mouth open.
Is he going to eat me?
No. He likes you. That's worse. Now he'll follow you everywhere.
Hask asked to see the village. I couldn't refuse. So I walked him through it myself, and prayed.
Glasshouses. In the north. How clever.
And the mill turns. I was told the mill here hadn't turned in ten years.
I read a book about it.
You read a great many books, Lord Lucan.
There wasn't much else to do. I'm a zero.
Then we reached the south field, and he stopped walking.
Barley.
This far north.
He didn't say anything else. He didn't have to.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighteen, coming soon.
